gauss: Genome Analysis Using Summary Statistics

Source: R/gauss-package.R
gauss-package.Rd

Analyses summary statistics from genome-wide association studies of cohorts with mixed ancestry, against an external reference panel of 32,953 samples drawn from 29 populations. The panel is read directly off disk by position, so it is never loaded into memory and is not distributed with the package.

Details

The entry points fall into four groups:

Imputation of unmeasured variants

dist for a single population or superpopulation, distmix for an arbitrary ancestry mixture.

Gene-level association

jepeg and jepegmix, which aggregate functional annotations into a single statistic per gene.

Region-level association

qcat and qcatmix.

Ancestry and linkage disequilibrium

afmix and zmix estimate mixing proportions from the study's own allele frequencies or Z-scores; computeLD returns the ancestry-informed LD matrix the other functions use internally.

Functions whose name ends in mix take a pop_wgt_df of mixing proportions and are read positionally: the first column must name the population and the second must carry its weight. See data(PGC2_SCZ_ANC_Prop) for the expected shape.

References

Lee D, Williamson VS, Bigdeli TB, Riley BP, Fanous AH, Vladimirov VI, Bacanu SA (2015). DIST: direct imputation of summary statistics for unmeasured SNPs. Bioinformatics 31(19):3099-3104. doi:10.1093/bioinformatics/btv348
